newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won closes lower, further fall seen.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won closes lower, further fall seen.

text.p: The won closed lower against the dollar on Tuesday as demand for the U.S. unit continued to strengthen, dealers said.
But the Bank of Korea's supply of $1 billion on Monday to local banks limited the dollar's steep rise.
The won closed at 888.70 after opening at an intraday high of 888.20. It touched 888.90, the lowest level since the nation launched the market average system in March 1990.
"The central bank's dollar supply helped support the won. But the basic sentiment for the dollar has not changed," said a foreign bank dealer.
The market was forecast to test the 890 level on Wednesday. The won's mid-rate was expected to be pegged at 888.70 on Wednesday, compared with 887.30 today.

Dealers said the won's weakness stemmed from the nation's widening trade deficit. The reopening of a prosecution probe into a loan scandal involving Hanbo Steel Co also dampened sentiment for the won by adding to the nation's economic woes.
A domestic bank dealer forecast trading would range from 888.00 to 889.50 on Wednesday, while a foreign bank dealer put it between 888.50 and 889.30.
